rules.name: Unsafe client-side DOM or React HTML sink
rules.description: Unsafe client-side DOM or React HTML sink (dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML =, outerHTML =, document.write, or eval) receives dynamic input without sanitization, leading to client-side Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).
rules.remediation_example: element.textContent = sanitize(userInput); // avoid raw HTML injection sinks

rules.name: Hardcoded secrets or credentials in web configuration or source
rules.description: Hardcoded API key, token, private key or database password committed in .env, JavaScript, TypeScript, PHP, Dockerfile (ENV/ARG), or docker-compose.yml file.
rules.remediation_example: Inject secrets dynamically at runtime via Docker secrets, KMS, or secret manager rather than committing in files.

rules.name: Unsafe PHP code execution or shell injection sink
rules.description: Direct execution of untrusted input in PHP dynamic evaluation or shell execution sinks (eval, shell_exec, system, passthru, exec with $_GET/$_POST/$_REQUEST).
rules.remediation_example: Avoid dynamic code execution and use parameterized functions or escapeshellarg().

rules.name: Container runs as root user or lacks non-root USER instruction
rules.description: Dockerfile explicitly sets USER root or does not declare a non-root USER instruction, allowing container processes to run with full host-root capabilities upon container breakout.
rules.remediation_example:
RUN groupadd -r appuser && useradd -r -g appuser appuser
USER appuser

rules.name: Unpinned base image or insecure remote ADD in Dockerfile
rules.description: Dockerfile uses an unpinned ':latest' base image or fetches untrusted remote files via 'ADD http://', risking supply chain poisoning and non-reproducible builds.
rules.remediation_example:
FROM python:3.11.8-slim-bookworm
# Use COPY and curl/wget with checksum verification instead of ADD http
